entries.prompt: Edit target is image 1 (the wall atlas). Images 2 and 3 are EXISTING GAME ART STYLE REFERENCES ONLY: image 2 is the game's real 64x128 entrance-door sprite, image 3 is its real 64x128 stocked shelf sprite. DO NOT redraw or output the reference door or shelf. Re-render the 16 wall pieces in image 1 so they belong to precisely the same pixel-art game as images 2 and 3. Preserve all sixteen architectural piece identities, 4x4 order, ivory plaster / teal stripe / charcoal skirting, full-wall vs low-wall distinctions, corners, caps and empty door openings. Important correction: previous walls are too smoothly rendered and densely shaded. Use the references' very small logical pixel grid: each sprite has a maximum logical canvas of 64x128, visibly chunky square pixels, one-pixel dark warm-brown contour, compact 3-4 flat tone clusters per material, simple upper-left baked light, no gradient, no blur, no continuous shading, no ambient occlusion halo, no shadow under or around sprites, no glossy 3D look, no voxel render. Exactly 2:1 isometric geometry matching the reference sprites, verticals upright, repeated wall segments the same length, door opening compatible with the reference door height. Keep transparent unused canvas and matching foot baselines. If displayed at larger size, render by integer nearest-neighbour scale ONLY: never create extra small subpixels, anti-aliasing or textured noise. 4 columns x4 rows with clear non-overlapping frames; no text, grid lines, floor tiles, furniture or people. Background must be truly transparent; solid sprite interiors fully opaque and clean binary-alpha pixel silhouette. The atlas is a visual candidate to be fitted to the existing 64x32 footprint grid, not a new art direction.

Create a complementary modular GLASS WINDOW sprite atlas for the game in the supplied images. Image 1 is a supporting art-style reference: the freshly adjusted cream/teal wall atlas. Image 2 is the ORIGINAL existing game entrance-door sprite, and image 3 is the ORIGINAL existing shelf sprite; their chunky small-resolution pixel grid and dark brown contour must be the strongest art-style references. Output ONLY the new window atlas, never copy the reference sprites into it. One transparent PNG containing exactly 8 distinct isolated window modules arranged 4 columns x2 rows, no text or labels or grid lines. Row1: four orientations (front-left, front-right, rear-left, rear-right) of the shop's low street-facing glass facade module: ivory sill below, teal accent stripe across the sill at the SAME height as the low walls, graphite baseboard, grey aluminium vertical mullions, clear pale-blue glass with just one or two square reflection marks, aluminium top rail. Height and modular length should match the low-wall family. Row2: inside-corner window junction, outside-corner window junction, left terminating window post and right terminating window post; same materials, lattice and height. True 2:1 isometric orthographic, square hard pixel steps, maximum 64x128 logical frame per simple module, compact flat pixel clusters, 3-4 tones per material, one-logical-pixel dark warm-brown contour, no gradient, no diffuse shadows, no ambient occlusion, no blur, no smooth high-resolution 3D rendering. Left-upper baked light matches the ORIGINAL game sprites. Keep clear transparent margins and a common foot baseline per row, no floor or scenery. Fully transparent background outside silhouette; any glass appearance should be represented by discrete flat pale blue pixel colors, not photorealistic transparency or reflections. New image is a candidate atlas that will be fitted to the existing game's 64x32 ground footprint.
entries.cleanup_prompt: Edit ONLY image 1, the 8-sprite window atlas. Preserve the exact eight window identities, 4x2 layout, cream/teal/grey/pale-blue palette, proportions, positions, common baseline and isometric projection. Correction required: remove ALL stray red pixels, red/grey fringing, jagged halo contamination outside the dark brown outline. Remove any soft ambient-occlusion glow or cast shadow around the sprites. The background outside every silhouette must be fully transparent clean alpha, and the opaque window frames and blue glass must have a crisp hard pixel boundary, no partial-alpha speckling. Keep the dark brown contour and flat pixel colors consistent with the existing cozy game art. Do not add, remove or redesign any component; no labels or background. The result should look like clean isolated pixel-art game sprite cutouts.

entries.prompt: Produce ONE new transparent pixel-art DOOR STATE atlas derived from the supplied existing game sprites. Image1 is the original shop entrance door. Image2 is the original production-room door with small green round details. Image3 is the original wooden warehouse door with mint trim. Image4 is a supporting reference for the new cream/teal wall family. Highest priority: preserve each original door's recognizable design, wood colors, mint/teal accents, dark brown pixel contours, height-to-width proportions and pixel density. No replacement modern sliding glass door, no new signs, no labels. Output exactly 24 separate sprites arranged in 3 rows and 8 columns. Row1 the existing SHOP ENTRANCE DOOR, row2 the existing PRODUCTION DOOR, row3 the existing WAREHOUSE DOOR. Each row columns in this order: front-left closed, front-left open, front-right closed, front-right open, rear-left closed, rear-left open, rear-right closed, rear-right open. Treat each adjacent pair as an animation pair: the fixed jamb, threshold, lintel and foot anchor must be IDENTICAL between closed and open; only the door leaf rotates about its existing hinge to show an unobstructed dark empty doorway. The open leaf is a thin pixel-art panel swung to the side, never detach or shift the jamb, never replace the opening with a window, never add stairs or a floor slab. Match original 2:1 isometric orthographic axes (1:2 pixel staircase), verticals upright, no camera perspective. Each pair gets equal canvas space with enough transparent margin for the open leaf. Logical original door drawing is roughly 64x128 pixels; extend canvas margins for open state while keeping door art the SAME logical pixel size as closed. Chunky pixel-art outlines, flat 3-4-tone color clusters, upper-left baked light. Absolutely no smooth gradients, no ambient occlusion halo, no cast ground shadows, no blur, no antialiasing, no photorealistic or glossy 3D style. Clean transparent background, hard silhouettes, no red edge fringes or colored background residue, solid opaque sprite interiors. No characters, products, furniture, grass, checkerboard, grid lines, labels or watermarks. This is an animation-state candidate sheet for existing game assets, with recognizable original door designs.
